Version of record: J Creat Behav 58(1), 128-136, epub 11 Jan 2024. No PDF or markdown on file (retrieval status not_obtained).
source.title_on_document: The Language of Creativity: Evidence from Humans and Large Language Models

supplement.where: The text cites no supplement; PMC metadata flags has-supplement = no. Data available from the corresponding author on request (Data Availability Statement).

paper_design_summary: Fifty Prolific participants each wrote six five-sentence stories from three-word prompts (300 stories). The authors also generated 300 stories with GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) and 120 with GPT-4 from the same prompts. An independent sample of 240 Prolific raters scored the stories for creativity on a 1-5 scale (12 ratings per story), and GPT-4 also rated each story; mixed models compare creativity by source and relate it to semantic diversity (DSI) and perceptual detail. No participant used AI.

studies.label: Human vs GPT-3 vs GPT-4 short stories (five-sentence creative story task)

participants.exclusions: Two outlier observations exceeding four standard deviations from the mean were removed (the paper does not say which stories).
participants.who: 50 human story writers recruited on Prolific, aged 18-35, native English speakers (300 human stories); 300 GPT-3 stories and 120 GPT-4 stories (corpus). Separate sample of 240 Prolific raters scored creativity.
participants.quote: Our sample of human participants (n = 50) was recruited online via Prolific.

ai_tool.how_used: AI generated stories on its own from the same prompts (temperature .65-.80, frequency and presence penalty 1 for GPT-3); GPT-4 also served as a creativity rater. No person used AI.

task.description: Five-sentence creative story task: write a short story of about five sentences that includes all three cue words; six prompts (three semantically close, three distant).
task.duration: 5 min per story for human writers

outcomes.name: Human-rated creativity, GPT-3 vs human stories
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean of 12 Prolific raters' 1-5 creativity scores per story; mixed model with condition as predictor, controlling for prompt and word count.

contrasts.reported: human vs. GPT-3: β = .07, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.16], t = 1.59, p = .11; R2 = .39 (a human story scores 0.07 points higher than a GPT-3 story of the same length and prompt)
contrasts.locator: NIH author manuscript PMC11065427, Results, paragraph 3 (S6/P17).

outcomes.name: Human-rated creativity, GPT-4 vs human stories (pooled model)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same human creativity ratings; model pooling human, GPT-3, and GPT-4 stories with human stories as reference.

contrasts.reported: compared to human stories, both GPT-3 (t = −1.66, p = .10) and GPT-4 (t = 1.98, p = .05) tend to score lower in creativity, though this difference was not significant (the GPT-4 t is printed positive while the text says lower)
contrasts.locator: NIH author manuscript PMC11065427, Results, paragraph 4 (S6/P18).

outcomes.name: GPT-4-rated creativity, GPT-3 vs human stories
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4 as judge: one 1-5 creativity score per story using the human raters' instructions; human-GPT-4 rating correlation r = .65 across all stories.

contrasts.reported: human stories were rated as significantly more creative (assessed by GPT) as compared to computer-generated stories (β = .14, 95% CI [0.02, 0.25], t = 2.36, p = .02)
contrasts.locator: NIH author manuscript PMC11065427, Results, paragraph 6 (S6/P20).

outcomes.name: GPT-4-rated creativity, GPT-4 vs human stories (pooled model)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4 creativity ratings; model pooling human, GPT-3, and GPT-4 stories with human stories as reference. Same model gives GPT-3 vs human β = −.14, 95% CI [−0.25, −0.02], t = 2.36, p = .02.

contrasts.reported: GPT-4 stories scored significantly higher (β = .76, 95% CI [0.60, 0.91], t = 9.74, p < .001) on GPT ratings of creativity
contrasts.locator: NIH author manuscript PMC11065427, Results, paragraph 7 (S6/P21).

eligibility.reason: Stories written by 50 recruited human participants without AI are compared with stories generated independently by GPT-3 and GPT-4; no person was assigned to AI assistance, so this is AI-versus-human output context (Methods, S1/P7-P9). The number of writers retained in the analyses is not reported after two outliers were removed, so criterion 2 remains unclear (Statistical Analyses, S5/P14). Creativity was scored on the stories by human raters and GPT-4 (Creativity Assessment, S2/P10-P11).

one_line_finding: Lay raters scored 300 GPT-3 stories about as creative as 300 human stories (human minus GPT-3 β = .07, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.16], p = .11) and 120 GPT-4 stories not significantly different from human ones (t = 1.98, p = .05), while GPT-4 as judge rated GPT-4 stories higher than human stories (β = .76, 95% CI [0.60, 0.91]) (PMC author manuscript, Results).
